title: Finite classical raw realization and normalized point comparison
statement: Fix a finite-field datum D, a prime l different from its characteristic, a normalized lisse realization family a whose point and pullback comparisons satisfy PointNormalized and PullNormalized, and a continuous rational realization family b. There exists a finite classical raw realization Family s relative to a and b, with PointComparison at every finite coefficient field E and separated finite-type geometric base W. Family includes the quotient/limit integral equivalence, degree-zero constructible raw functor, full faithfulness, sf ordinary-module comparison, identity-induced PBC comparison, specified-isomorphism lift, and the finite classical fibre formulas. No operations, coherence, common-stage descent or arbitrary restricted-heart fibre is asserted. Interfaces: [def-zl-classical-raw-lisse-realization-data], [def-zl-classical-raw-lisse-point-fibres], [def-real-lisse-point-normalization], [def-real-lisse-pullback-normalization], [def-per-continuous-rational-realization-data]. Additional interface owners: [def-real-lisse-realization-data], [def-per-continuous-rational-realization-data], [def-weil-finite-field-fiber], [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension], [def-per-adic-base-stages].

proof.text: Transport the reduction equivalence of completed_system_comparison along its residue-normalized coefficient isomorphism to the specified completed coefficient ring. Its inverse is the actual limit of the pulled-back finite levels; transport its quotient cokernels, limit cone, unit and counit projections. The inverse limit is locally finite free, so its degree-zero complex satisfies the one-stratum integral stratified-perfect criterion, including the etale-origin witnesses. Apply the actual degree-zero functor and scalar localization on compatible-family maps to define the raw heart functor.

proof.text: The rational realization formulas identify this with ordinary localization of the lattice, on objects and every fraction. Full faithfulness follows from the completed system comparison. Use the identity-induced coefficient equivalence and continuous realization to obtain the PBC comparison; full faithfulness lifts a specified module isomorphism and its inverse, giving its prescribed lift equation. Evaluate the completion cone at each geometric point and localize to obtain the finite fibre comparison.

proof.text: Evaluation preserves limits, so its maps are the inverse limits of the actual finite stalk maps. Use the normalized completed-pullback gamma inverse, the exact-functor H0 comparisons and identity-on-sections coefficient transport to construct the intrinsic fibre bridge. The point and pullback normalizations of a identify its composite with the same limit-of-stalks comparison. Precomposition of pointed etale neighbourhoods commutes with the cone projections, proving transport for every point automorphism.
